successCriteria.description: The Holiday interface is defined as a standalone data interface (not extending BaseEntity) with exactly four fields: id (string), date (Date), name (string), country (string). It compiles under strict TypeScript without importing BaseEntity.

The IHolidayRepository interface exposes exactly two read-only methods: findByDateRange(startDate: Date, endDate: Date) returning Promise<Holiday[]>, and findByYear(year: number) returning Promise<Holiday[]>. No create/update/delete methods exist on the interface.

PgHolidayRepository implements IHolidayRepository and uses the shared pg pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts. findByDateRange queries the holidays table with an inclusive date range (date >= startDate AND date <= endDate) and returns matching Holiday entities. findByYear queries rows whose date falls within the requested calendar year and returns matching Holiday entities.

The repository's row mapper returns Date objects for the date field that are directly consumable by countBusinessDays(startDate, endDate, holidays: Date[]) — i.e., each returned Holiday's date is a JS Date whose local date components (year/month/day) match the stored holiday date, so isSameDay() comparison in day-count.ts works correctly.

The barrel file src/shared/holidays/index.ts re-exports the Holiday type, the IHolidayRepository type, and the PgHolidayRepository class, so consumers can import all three from the single module entry point.

Jest unit tests at tests/unit/shared/holidays/holiday.repository.test.ts mock the shared pg pool and cover: findByDateRange returning matching rows, findByDateRange returning an empty array when no rows match, findByDateRange rejecting on a pool error, findByYear returning matching rows, findByYear returning an empty array, and findByYear rejecting on a pool error. All tests pass under the project's Jest configuration.

constraints: No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards instead (HARNESS.json constraint no-any, severity high). The HolidayRow interface and row mapper must be fully typed.

All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001 / HARNESS.json no-direct-db-outside-repository, severity critical). PgHolidayRepository is the sole database access point for the holidays table; no inline SQL elsewhere.

The repository must let database errors propagate as rejected promises without try/catch wrapping — matching the established convention across employee, policy, balance, and leave repositories (GP-006: no unhandled promise rejections at the caller level, but the repository itself does not swallow errors).

Strict TypeScript must pass (no implicit any, strict null checks). The Holiday interface, IHolidayRepository interface, PgHolidayRepository class, and barrel must all compile cleanly under `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit).
Test files must use the project's Jest convention — `*.test.ts` under `tests/` matching the configured testMatch, NOT `.spec.ts`. The Jest config must not be modified.
outOfScope: No create/update/delete operations on the holidays table — the repository is read-only (findByDateRange and findByYear only). Holiday data ingestion/management is deferred.

No country-based filtering at the repository layer — the country field is stored and returned but not used as a query parameter in this phase. Multi-country filtering logic is deferred to the Phase 10 leave service consumer.
No database migration for the holidays table — schema creation is out of scope for this phase. The repository assumes the holidays table exists with columns id, date, name, country.

No service, controller, or routes layer for holidays — this phase delivers only the model, repository interface, repository implementation, barrel, and unit tests. The leave service (Phase 10) will consume IHolidayRepository.

entityInvariants.invariant: Holiday is reference data, not a domain aggregate — it does not extend BaseEntity and carries no createdAt/updatedAt lifecycle timestamps. It is immutable from the application's perspective (read-only access only in this phase).

Every Holiday returned by the repository must have a non-null date that is a valid JS Date object whose local date components correspond to the actual public holiday date, ensuring compatibility with countBusinessDays' isSameDay() comparison.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only query with no side effects. Returns an empty array (not null) when no holidays fall within the inclusive range. Database errors propagate as rejected promises without swallowing.
Read-only query with no side effects. Returns an empty array (not null) when no holidays exist for the requested calendar year. Database errors propagate as rejected promises without swallowing.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: PgHolidayRepository must import the shared `pool` from src/shared/db/connection.ts — the same pool instance used by all other repositories (employee, policy, balance, leave). No separate database connection or Pool instantiation.

The repository's returned Holiday.date values must be directly passable as the `holidays: Date[]` argument to countBusinessDays. The date objects must have local date components (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate) matching the stored holiday date, because countBusinessDays uses isSameDay() which compares local-time getters — not UTC.

The repository implementation must follow the established pattern: define a private *Row interface for DB columns, a private rowTo* mapper function, use pool.query<RowType>(sql, params) accessing result.rows, and have the class implement the interface (PgHolidayRepository implements IHolidayRepository). Errors propagate as rejected promises without try/catch.

The unit test must follow the established test pattern: jest.mock the shared db connection module, import pool after the mock, cast pool.query as jest.Mock, use makeRow()/makeEntity() helper factories with overrides, structure as describe('PgHolidayRepository') with nested describe blocks per method, call jest.clearAllMocks() in beforeEach, and cast mock resolved values with `as never`.

The Holiday interface must NOT extend BaseEntity. BaseEntity defines id/createdAt/updatedAt; Holiday is reference data with only id/date/name/country and no lifecycle timestamps. base-entity.interface.ts is read for awareness only — it is not imported by the holidays module.

integrationPoints.why: The repository's primary consumer contract: findByDateRange returns Holiday[] whose .date values are extracted and passed as the holidays: Date[] argument to countBusinessDays. The Phase 10 leave service will call findByDateRange, map results to Date[], and invoke countBusinessDays for business-day calculation.
PgHolidayRepository depends on the shared Pool instance for all database queries, consistent with every other repository in the codebase.

The leave service constructor will accept IHolidayRepository to fetch holidays for a leave request's date range, enabling accurate business-day counting that excludes public holidays per binding rule 2.
